This Gorgeous Aussie Tiny Home Is All About Warmth, Comfort, and Indoor-Outdoor Living
20 photos
Photo: LJM Tiny Homes
Sometimes, too much focus on minimalism and simplicity in tiny home design can result in living spaces that feel cold and sterile. Clean lines, neutral colors, and uncluttered spaces are all well and good, but a home needs warmth and personality to feel inviting.
Designers can keep a tiny home simple and clutter-free without making it feel dull by using natural wood grains, layered materials, and soft textiles, and ditching harsh overhead lights in favor of warm mood lighting. The Cooloola tiny house does all that and achieves the right balance between minimalism and liveliness.
This beautiful home on wheels is one of the latest creations from Australian builder LJM Tiny Homes and transforms minimalist design into a form of art by integrating warm wood tones, curved furniture, hidden and layered ambient lighting, and generous openings to the outdoors. It combines a contemporary exterior with an open-plan living area, a generous U-shaped kitchen, and two sleeping lofts, providing a highly livable dwelling for a couple or even a small family.
From the outside, the Cooloola has all the attributes of a genuine Australian tiny home . It features white Colorbond steel cladding and ample glazing, which combine with a skillion roofline, black window frames, and a wooden deck to give the home a contemporary appearance.
Photo: LJM Tiny Homes What makes this model truly stand out is the way it connects indoor and outdoor living. One glance through the large tri-fold entry door is enough to spot the gorgeous living area that opens up completely to the front deck. Next to it, a wide bistro-style window acts as a pass-through bar from the kitchen, creating a serving counter where you can enjoy breakfast, coffee, or a casual drink in the open air.
Apart from adding bar stools under that large servery window, owners can also put patio furniture on the spacious wooden deck, transforming it into an integrated outdoor living area, perfect for evenings with friends. With such an arrangement, the deck would feel like a natural extension of the kitchen and living room.
The abundance of glazing creates an open feel inside as well, while also pulling in views of the surrounding natural landscape. The team at LJM Tiny Homes created a warm aesthetic and welcoming ambiance by using woods of different shades, soft textiles, and beautiful decor. Light-colored plywood panels cover the walls and ceilings, while also accentuating the darker walnut-toned cabinetry that adds depth and richness to the living space.
Photo: LJM Tiny Homes The central living area is the kind of space that invites relaxation with a book in hand. It is furnished with a beautiful L-shaped sofa with rounded edges, white cushions, and subtle lighting under the seating, making it look like it’s floating. The sofa is paired with a modern round coffee table and faces the large folding door for beautiful views.
Another distinctive feature of this welcoming lounge is a custom-built dark wood shelving unit with an arched top section, which provides display space for books, framed photos, and decorative items. Lighting also plays an important role in creating a more inviting atmosphere than in other tiny houses . During the day, light pours in not only through the main door but also through a skylight just above the lounge, and at night, indirect lighting and accent lamps help create a soft, candle-like glow.
The massive U-shaped kitchen that wraps around one end of the ground floor is a chef’s dream. The wraparound countertops provide plenty of workspace for food preparation, and the layout keeps the cooking zone distinct from the living area without completely separating it.
Photo: LJM Tiny Homes One section of the countertop doubles as a breakfast bar, which combines with the large servery window to enhance the seamless indoor-outdoor flow. This setup makes the kitchen quite versatile, making it suitable for everything from cooking everyday meals to relaxed outdoor entertaining.
The wood-toned cabinetry is paired with a stainless steel countertop that adds a tinge of industrial vibe to the culinary space, and there are no upper cabinets to obstruct the views. In terms of functionality, the kitchen is equipped with a gas range and oven, a full-sized refrigerator, a dishwasher, a sink, and a pull-out pantry.
A narrow hallway leads from the living area to the bathroom and the stairs to one of the sleeping lofts. The bathroom is quite spacious for a tiny house and includes a full shower with a glass door and a window to the outside, a stylish suspended sink, and a composting toilet. Storage is integrated behind the toilet, while a large cabinet covers the opposite wall.
Photo: LJM Tiny Homes For sleeping, the Cooloola has two lofts positioned at either end of the house. Both are typical tiny house lofts with limited headroom, but are quite cozy and accommodate queen-size mattresses. While the loft above the bathroom is reached via the storage-integrated staircase, the one above the kitchen is accessed by a simple wooden ladder.
At 8.4 meters (27.5 feet) long, 2.5 meters (8.2 feet) wide, and 4.3 meters (14.1 feet) tall, this home is Rover-compliant (the Australian Road Standards), which makes it an appealing option for those who want to travel or change location frequently.
It sits on a custom-built, tri-axle flatbed steel trailer with adjustable leg supports, electric brakes on all six wheels, and a breakaway system, and structurally, it is built with Truecore steel framing, including the internal walls, with an insulated composite subfloor and insulated walls and ceiling.
With its warm aesthetic, practical features, and indoor-outdoor living setup, the Cooloola proves tiny homes can be a pleasure to live in. Price-wise, this model starts from AUD $83,600, which is about USD $57,850 at current exchange rates.
